They cannot just set up a hidden spy camera and spy on you as in that case you would have no knowledge of said communication and therefore no ability to consent to it. No, this includes all communications over their services.

The section states:

You agree that Comcast and its agents may monitor and record any telephone calls or other voice, data or image communications that are transmitted between:

(1) Comcast and its agents

and

(2) you, your agents, any user of your Service(s) or Equipment, or any user of any phone numbers associated with your account.

When you call your mother (you do call your mother right :) ) your communication is between you and your mother, not you and Comcast, so Comcast does not have the right to record it. Similarly if you email someone (other than Comcast), or text, or visit a non-comcast webpage, or whatever.

In many states it would be illegal for them to record your calls without informing the other party first (two-party consent requirement). This section is merely notifying you as one party and they are the second party so they satisfy the two-party consent requirement only when you are communicating with them. At least that's my understanding (IANAL).
